name: task-execution-cadence
body: The cadence for executing one plan task to a durable "done" under the branch graph's content-identity staleness guard: one task per implementer session; the implementer commits its work and returns; the coordinator quick-verifies the commit against the task's target, scans so the recorded HEAD catches up, then resumes the session only to mark done (`apg_plan_done`) and note (`apg_plan_note`). It exists because the guard refuses every plan/review mutation unless the recorded HEAD matches the working tree (same sha and clean), so "mark done then commit" and "mark done while dirty" are both impossible; the cadence is the ordering that survives the guard. Target-less tasks (spikes, gates, file-level aggregates) that write nothing and leave the tree clean need no commit/scan — their stated condition is the completion signal — and their tasks are ordered after the units they aggregate, with gate tasks last. This is the ordering discipline for MUTATING the plan; it is distinct from `domain.entity.graph-first-navigation`, the ordering discipline for querying the graph.
